hints: Focus on what water does in hydrolysis, it uses a lone pair on oxygen to attack a slightly positive carbon.
Compare the C-Br bond with the C-Cl bond, one is longer and weaker and so breaks more easily in the rate determining step.
Put the two ideas together, the faster haloalkane plus attack by a lone pair donor tells you both columns of the table.
walkthrough:
**Spot what hydrolysis of a haloalkane is**

Think of water as a nucleophile. The oxygen has lone pairs and is attracted to the electron deficient carbon attached to the halogen.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{X} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{HX}$$

**Decide which bond breaks faster**

The key bond to break is C-X. The C-Br bond is longer and weaker than the C-Cl bond, so it needs less energy to break.

Bond strength: $\text{C-Br} < \text{C-Cl}$ so bromoethane reacts more rapidly.

**Name the mechanism type**

A nucleophile ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) replaces the halide leaving group ($\text{Br}^-$ or $\text{Cl}^-$). That is nucleophilic substitution, not electrophilic substitution.

So the answer is bromoethane hydrolyses faster by nucleophilic substitution.

options.A: Half right and half wrong. Bromoethane is indeed faster because the C-Br bond is weaker, but electrophilic substitution is incorrect. Water is supplying electrons, not accepting them, so it acts as a nucleophile.
options.B: Correct on both parts. Bromoethane is faster because the C-Br bond breaks more easily than C-Cl, and water acting as a lone pair donor to replace $\text{Br}^-$ is classic nucleophilic substitution to form ethanol.
options.C: Wrong on both parts. Chloroethane is slower because the C-Cl bond is stronger and harder to break, and electrophilic substitution describes attack by an electron acceptor, which is the opposite of what water does here.
options.D: Mechanism is right but compound is wrong. Nucleophilic substitution is correct, but chloroethane is slower. Students who think smaller chlorine leaves more easily pick this, but bond strength controls rate, and C-Br is weaker.
